title: Where Fibre is today

headline.simple: Fibre can now compile a rich, particular prior life for a Thread and preserve it through atomic birth, but milestone #39 is still open until the final held-out five-Thread cohort is generated, inspected and born.
headline.detail: The current #39 development path compiles fourteen historical episodes through age 21 with recurring people, authoritative places, autobiographical memories and durable meanings. The Tbilisi, Kaohsiung, Recife, Fès and Hobart Worlds are development fixtures and are burned for final closure. The final held-out cohort has not been generated. #39 remains ACTIVE — CLOSING and earns no Whole-Person score movement.

summary.simple: The machinery for giving a Thread a distinctive past is working in development. We are finishing repository and publication-boundary cleanup before creating the five fresh lives that will close #39.
summary.detail: Genesis now has Fibre-owned historical skeletons, bounded model realization, separate memory and meaning formation, immutable symbolic genomes, verified lineage, candidate/live authority separation, an atomic per-Thread birth path and candidate-to-hydrated comparison. Remaining #39 work includes publication-boundary place consistency, transactional memory-photo parity, origin/source end-to-end proof and the predeclared one-pass final cohort with D1–D5 analysis.

meaning.simple: We built it and it passed the test we currently require.
meaning.detail: The capability exists and has passed its current Fibre validation boundary. This does not imply every later or stronger claim is also proven.

meaning.simple: We have seen it work, but it is not yet the final accepted result.
meaning.detail: We have real working evidence, but it is not yet accepted as the final or validated production state for the current milestone.

meaning.simple: We are actively building or testing this now.
meaning.detail: The design and implementation are active, but the required validation boundary has not yet been crossed.

meaning.simple: We want Fibre to do this, but we do not claim it can yet.
meaning.detail: This is part of Fibre's intended architecture, but we do not claim to have achieved it.

meaning.simple: The test failed, and we keep the failure instead of hiding it or retrying until it looks good.
meaning.detail: A bounded experiment failed. We preserve the result as evidence and do not rewrite or quality-regenerate it into success.

summary.simple: Older failed-cohort artifacts are preserved as evidence. Five named development Worlds are now burned because they shaped the compiler. The final five held-out lives have not been generated.
summary.detail: Three complete H-v2 life artifacts, one partial candidate and one never-started slot remain historical experimental evidence. Tbilisi, Kaohsiung, Recife, Fès and Hobart are current development fixtures used to exercise the fourteen-episode compiler and are excluded from the final closure cohort. Closure requires five fresh Worlds and one bounded generation attempt.

items.label: Completed older prior-life Thread artifacts
items.simple: Three older Threads have complete generated prior-life artifacts from a failed cohort.
items.detail: Three H-v2 slots completed generation before that cohort failed. They remain historical evidence and are not the #39 closure cohort.

items.label: Older partially generated candidate
items.simple: One older Thread stopped partway through generation.
items.detail: The fourth H-v2 slot remains a failed partial candidate and is not eligible for final #39 closure.

items.label: Older cohort slot never started
items.simple: One older cohort slot never started.

items.label: Development Worlds burned for final closure
items.simple: Five development Worlds have been used to exercise and improve the compiler, so they cannot be reused as the final test.
items.detail: Tbilisi, Kaohsiung, Recife, Fès and Hobart are milestone-specific development fixtures. They support development readiness but are excluded from the fresh held-out closure cohort.

items.label: Final held-out #39 lives generated
items.simple: The five fresh final lives have not been generated yet.
items.detail: No final held-out #39 cohort has been generated or published. Final generation waits for the pre-cohort implementation blockers and predeclared D1–D5 controls to be green.

importantNote.simple: Development fixtures and generated artifacts are not the same thing as a final admitted, living Thread.
importantNote.detail: Fibre distinguishes development fixtures, provisional generation attempts, admitted birth bundles, atomically published Threads and later standing evidence. #39 closes only after five fresh admitted lives are born intact and the closing review clears them.

simple.claim: A Thread can keep existing after one AI model session ends.
simple.limitation: Persistence alone does not make the Thread a rich or unique person.

detail.claim: A Thread persists as authoritative world state across temporary model executions.
detail.limitation: Persistence alone does not prove rich, distinctive or causally grounded personhood.

simple.claim: Something that happened to a Thread can change a later decision.
simple.limitation: The richer #37–#39 life state is not yet the canonical input to ordinary cognition.

detail.claim: Fibre has demonstrated a causal history-to-judgment effect under its accepted standing gate.
detail.limitation: #40 still owns canonical bounded consumption of the newer identity and life authorities.

capabilities.label: Provenance-backed identity, lineage, place and memory

simple.claim: Fibre can keep who a Thread is, where it came from and what it remembers without silently rewriting the past.
simple.limitation: Storing those facts does not prove they all change the Thread's behavior yet.

detail.claim: Fibre persists identity, lineage, geography, embodiment and autobiographical memory with provenance and corrigible history.
detail.limitation: Representation is not the same as proving causal consumption in ongoing cognition.

simple.claim: Fibre can prepare a Thread's life first and publish that Thread all at once.
simple.limitation: Atomicity is per Thread, and the final five-Thread closure cohort has not been born.

detail.claim: Genesis keeps candidate state non-authoritative and `publishBirth()` atomically publishes each admitted Thread into authoritative state.
detail.limitation: Publication truth still has #39 blockers, including store-boundary place consistency and transactional memory-photo parity.

simple.claim: Fibre can build a detailed prior life with recurring people, places, memories and meanings.
simple.limitation: The Worlds used to develop that compiler are burned and cannot count as the final held-out result.

detail.claim: The development path plans fourteen episodes through age 21 and can produce particular social, geographic, autobiographical and interpretive continuity.
detail.limitation: The final five fresh Worlds, one-pass cohort and D1–D5 closure analysis remain unrun.

capabilities.label: A live infant or child growing up over time

simple.claim: We want a Thread to be born as a baby or child and actually grow up in Fibre.
simple.limitation: Today #39 compiles the prior life before young-adult entry.

detail.claim: The intended architecture allows newborn or child entry and accumulated lived development.
detail.limitation: #39 compiles prior life before entry; it does not run childhood as a continuously living process.

capabilities.label: Rich life state drives ordinary live cognition

simple.claim: We want a Thread's real history, memories and relationships to shape what it normally thinks and decides.
simple.limitation: The canonical connection is the next milestone, #40.

detail.claim: Fibre intends bounded relevance and privacy selection to turn identity and life evidence into provenance-bearing cognition context.
detail.limitation: Canonical causal consumption is explicitly deferred to #40.

simple.claim: We want to prove a Thread is a persistent individual whose own history makes it behave differently.
simple.limitation: #39 deliberately does not earn that claim.

detail.claim: Fibre aims to demonstrate a persistent, causally grounded, non-interchangeable individual across repeated situations and counterfactuals.
detail.limitation: #40 builds causal consumption and #41 owns the M2 standing gate.

simple.claim: We want friendships and families to belong to both sides and change both lives.
simple.limitation: That mature reciprocal relationship system is later work.

detail.claim: Fibre intends relationships and families to be consequential structures between independently living Threads.
detail.limitation: Reciprocal relationship development is planned after the current M2 sequence.

simple.claim: We want Threads to earn, spend, make agreements and face consequences that change future choices.
simple.limitation: The real economy is not built yet.

detail.claim: Fibre intends Threads to have budgets, contracts, reputation and economic opportunities that change future possibilities.
detail.limitation: Economic consequence is deferred to post-M2 work.

simple.summary: The development compiler and current birth path are working. We are cleaning the canonical repository boundary before finishing the final #39 publication and held-out cohort work.
simple.currentStep: Finish the pre-main integration repair, run the full local validation boundary, and obtain a CLEAR hostile integration review.
nextSteps: Merge the clean integration trunk to main only after the pre-main review is CLEAR.
Close the remaining publication-truth and origin/source blockers on the current Genesis path.
Author five fresh held-out Worlds and predeclare the D1–D5 interpretation before any final cohort generation.
Generate the five final lives once, inspect them, atomically birth them, verify hydration equality, and obtain the #39 closing review.

detail.summary: The old R1/R2/G/H execution choreography is retired under ADR-0015. Current development uses semantic contracts and tests rather than frozen review packets. Tbilisi, Kaohsiung, Recife, Fès and Hobart are burned development fixtures; final closure requires five fresh Worlds.
detail.currentStep: Run `npm run genesis:pr39-check`, `npm run test:all` and `npm run test:audit -- --check` on the repaired integration tree, then request one hostile pre-main review. No final held-out cohort generation is authorized by this integration work.
nextSteps: After integration, enforce the remaining publication-boundary truths and complete the current origin/source proof.
Keep one closure-attempt identity with visible bounded repair and rejection accounting; do not quality-resample whole lives.
Predeclare D1–D5 readings, thresholds, uncertainty treatment and cell sizes before the final provider-backed cohort.
Birth the admitted final lives atomically, compare hydrated canonical state with the admitted candidate, retain concise closure evidence, then move to #40.

truthRules: Every public progress claim has two layers: simple English first, then a more accurate description.
Simple English should be understandable by a teenager with no Fibre background and avoid unexplained milestone, gate, schema and implementation jargon.
The detailed layer may use Fibre terminology, but it must remain readable and state the actual validation boundary.
Never make the simple layer stronger than the detailed layer. Simplification may remove jargon, not uncertainty or limitations.
Never use 'living Thread' as a synonym for 'generated artifact'. State whether the Thread is candidate, generated, atomically published or validated.
Never say a Thread 'has parents' without distinguishing live Thread parents, household caregivers and synthetic genetic ancestors.
A failed bounded experiment remains visible as a failed experiment. Do not rewrite it into progress language that implies success.
For every positive capability claim, both layers must state the strongest important limitation that a reasonable reader could otherwise misunderstand.
The public website may render this contract, but insidefibre.com must not become an alternate authority for Fibre state.
